headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0217 — SMTO couldn't read the text on a PDF page

html:
SMTO-EXE-0217 — SMTO couldn't read the text on a PDF page

GUID: cbf5d3f5-b524-53ff-94ef-b876acefcf3c
Slug: pdf-text-extraction-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO tried to pull the text out of a page in your PDF, but its PDF reader ran into a problem with that page. This isn't the same as a blank page, and your PDF wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the same conversation, ask SMTO to read the other pages separately, for example "Read pages 1 to 2 of report.pdf". One bad page stops the whole request, so asking for the other pages on their own still gets you their text.
  2. Ask SMTO to read the failed page with OCR, which recognizes text from a picture of the page, for example "Use OCR on page 3 of report.pdf". OCR reads the page as an image, so it can work when the page's built-in text can't be decoded.
  3. Open the PDF in another app, save or print it to a new PDF file, then ask SMTO to read the new copy. Re-saving often rebuilds the page data that SMTO's PDF reader couldn't handle.

What success looks like

  • SMTO replies with the text from that page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the PDF's name and the page number, to the person who manages SMTO. Only share the PDF itself if its contents are safe to share.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway PDF backend (pypdf) raised an unexpected error while extracting text from a page, so no text result was produced; this is different from a page that has no text.

What this means

  • Text extraction raised an exception outside the explicit decoded-stream bound, so no trustworthy extraction result was produced. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Text extraction raised an exception outside the explicit decoded-stream bound, so no trustworthy extraction result was produced.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected page and extraction diagnostics; distinguish failure from an image-only page before choosing OCR.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway log for the failed pdf.text request: Document.page_text in src/gateway_core/pdf/backend.py turns any unexpected pypdf error into text_extraction_failed. Retry with a narrower page selection, run the pdf.ocr operation on that page if Tesseract is available, or repair and re-save the PDF; report a reproducible file as a backend bug.
  • Inspect the failed page and parser evidence; use supported OCR only when it fits the intended source and requirement.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid extraction or separately requested supported OCR yields evidence with its actual method identified.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
